title: add-vpc-control-plane-terraform-multi-az-interface-endpoints-peering-route53
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds terraform modules and docs for multi-AZ VPC control plane provisioning including interface endpoints, security groups, peering, and Route53 integration. No runtime changes.
description: Context: This PR adds Terraform automation for provisioning the VPC-based private control plane used by Redwood Private installs. Motivation: customers deploying Private in regulated environments need a reproducible, multi-AZ networking topology that includes private interface endpoints, tight security groups, cross-account peering, and Route53 DNS delegation so the control plane remains reachable and auditable without exposing public endpoints. This change standardizes the topology, enables idempotent upgrades, and aligns the installer with our Dedicated/VPC networking expectations. What this PR does: - New module: modules/vpc-control-plane with submodules for subnets, interface endpoints (AWS Interface Endpoint configurations for SSM, KMS, ECR, STS), security groups (least-privilege rules for control plane components), cross-account peering resources and route propagation, and Route53 hosted zone creation + delegation records. - Multi-AZ: Default layout uses 3 AZs with public NAT gateways removed for control plane subnets; subnets are private with egress through shared NAT. - Interface endpoints: Adds support for aws_vpc_endpoint_interface with private DNS options and applied security groups; conditional creation for regions that support endpoints. - Peering: Cross-account VPC peering resources with automated route table updates and optional route53-peering zone records for private DNS resolution across customers and services. - Inputs/outputs: Clear variable surface for AZ count, cidr blocks, peering accounts, and hosted zone names. - Installer integration: Hooked into redwood-private-installer/terraform with a new workspace var and upgrade plan helper that marks expected drift for manual review. - Docs: Added examples and a migration guide (MIGRATE-VPC.md) for existing Private customers. Testing done: - Terraform plan/apply against a sandbox account (three AZs) - End-to-end DNS validation using temp zones and delegated records - Backend integration smoke tests for control plane components to ensure SSM/KMS endpoints reachable - Manual peering teardown/recreate to validate upgrade safety Checklist: - [x] Module and submodules implemented - [x] Integration with installer workspace and variables - [x] Unit tests for terraform (tflint, fmt) - [x] Manual sandbox apply/rollback validated - [x] Docs and migration guide added Notes: - This PR intentionally leaves S3 gateway endpoints optional (commented) because some customers prefer NAT egress. - We added a feature flag variable `enable_route53_peering` defaulting to false for customers that cannot accept cross-account DNS changes. Related: ENG-1923 (multi-AZ VPC control plane), SUP-4121 (customer migration request), ENG-1978 (installer upgrade flow). Please review network/security boundaries carefully.
commits: Add interface endpoints and security group rules
Implement peering resources and automated route table updates
Add tests and CI steps for terraform plan/apply in sandbox
diff_snippets:
modules/vpc-control-plane/interface_endpoints.tf: resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "ssm" {
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.${var.region}.ssm"
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  subnet_ids   = local.control_plane_subnets
  security_group_ids = [module.sg.control_plane_id]
  private_dns_enabled = true
}"

merge_commit_message:
Squash and merge: add vpc control plane terraform multi-az interface endpoints peering route53

Implements multi-AZ VPC control plane module, interface endpoints, peering, security groups, and docs. Links: ENG-1923, ENG-1978, SUP-4121
notes_for_ops: After merge: run terraform plan in customer's staging workspace with enable_route53_peering=false to validate resources before enabling peering.
When enabling route53 peering, coordinate with DNS owners for delegation records; use the provided sample runbook in MIGRATE-VPC.md.
Rollbacks: module includes lifecycle ignore_changes for peer status to make rolling back safer; manual peering delete may be required for some AWS accounts.
